interface.title: Exoplanet Data Visualization (Dash dashboard by dpaguba)
interface.stage_of_work: Exploratory data analysis and screening of a published catalogue
interface.what_it_is_for: Filter Kepler planet candidates by planet radius and host-star size and explore four charts, three coloured by a habitability class (promising/challenging/extreme), to find which planets and host stars look potentially habitable. The class comes from a fixed rule on planet temperature and planet radius (the README calls the radius test 'gravity'). The interface never shows the rule's thresholds.

data.note: The dashboard loads data by itself on startup. The live Asterank API is unreachable in the sandbox, so it used the bundled asterank_exo.csv. The replay could not confirm the fallback from the browser. The Data tab shows 25 pages of 40 rows (about 1,000 planets) with columns KOI, A, DEC, RSTAR, TSTAR, KMAG, TPLANET, T0, UT0, PER, RA, UPER, RPLANET, MSTAR. The habitability status and star-size class appear only as chart colours, not as table columns. The About tab gives a dictionary of the fields. How status is derived (from the source code, data/processor.py, per the reviewer; not visible anywhere in the interface): 'promising' means TPLANET is 200–400 K and RPLANET is 0.5–2 Earth radii; 'challenging' means one of the two is in range and the other is borderline; anything else is 'extreme'. The 'gravity' criterion is only a planet-radius cut, not a computed surface gravity. Caution when comparing charts by colour: the Relative Distance chart colours the classes differently (extreme purple, challenging red, promising teal) from the Celestial Sphere and Star Mass charts (extreme grey, challenging blue, promising green) (screens/030.webp).

tree.general: Screen a catalogue of candidate objects for those whose properties make them worth following up, and see how they relate to their host systems
tree.specific: Find which Kepler planets are 'promising' for habitability (TPLANET 200–400 K and RPLANET 0.5–2 Earth radii, a rule the interface does not display) and how their temperature, orbital distance, sky position and host-star mass and temperature compare with the rest

children.finding: Screening result: the promising planets are few (1 with similar-size stars and radius capped at about 10–12 Earth radii). Their hovered RPLANET values are about 1.5–2.0 (1.54, 1.64, 1.86, 1.92, 1.99), their Relative_dist (A/RSTAR) is below Earth's 1.0 (e.g. 0.695), and their host stars have low mass and are cool, at MSTAR about 0.4–0.9 and TSTAR about 3600–5300 K. Planets with radius above about 11 Earth radii are all 'extreme'.

open_fixes: A separate feature for rule-based class labelling was not added as an operable component. The rule is not visible or settable in the interface, and no run checked it against boundary planets. A new run should hover planets near 200/400 K and 0.5/2 Earth radii to confirm the thresholds and the 'challenging' definition.

A systematic comparison of habitability classes across star sizes (isolating 'promising' under each of small, similar and bigger, with the full radius range) needs a new run. The current run did this only for similar stars with a capped radius range, plus an unhovered small-star view.
Search, Deselect All, keyboard slider control and applying an empty star selection (f1 steps) appear only in the explorer's screens and were not tried in the replay; a new replay should confirm them.
